title: I built a Windows app to explore and compare Instagram data exports locally
summary:
Instagram gives you a ZIP when you request a copy of your data. I built InstagramTracker to make that archive easier to browse and to compare two exports from the same account.

The Windows preview lets you open the ZIP on your computer, see which categories it contains, and compare follower and following lists across two exports. You can do this without signing in to Instagram or uploading the ZIP. A missing entry shows a difference between the exports, but it doesn’t tell you why it disappeared.

The project is MIT-licensed. The Windows x64 preview is portable and the executable is unsigned.

https://github.com/KaanKaya17/InstagramTracker/blob/main/README.en.md

title: Daemons can now send traces to Vercel Tracing
summary:
Vercel Daemons can now send OpenTelemetry traces to Vercel Tracing, allowing you and your agents to inspect background worker operations alongside the rest of your project's traces.

Vercel provides each daemon with a Unix socket for receiving OTLP/HTTP traces and sets the socket's path in VERCEL_OTEL_SOCKET_PATH.

Upgrading @vercel/otel to version 2.3.0 or later enables automatic trace export for Node.js daemons using the default configuration. The SDK detects this socket and sends the spans your worker records to Vercel.

These spans are available through the Vercel CLI, which can search by service name within a project and return JSON for your agents.
